{"caption":"A three-stage self-questioning workflow converts environment exploration into candidate tasks and filters them through replay.","description":"A process diagram with three numbered stages. Across the top, a blue panel says, “I have a sandbox environment. There are locations and facilities on map...” and contains buttons labeled “Environment Profile” and “User Preference.” A gray right-pointing arrow labeled “Self-Questioning” leads to a dashed box holding repeated green “Query” and “Ref. Solution” pairs, followed by an ellipsis for more pairs.

Stage 1, “Exploration,” shows an agent walking through a gray road map containing several blue location or facility symbols, including building-like icons and a house. An orange route winds across the map and exits toward Stage 2. The panel is labeled “Walk in Environment.”

Stage 2, “Task Synthesis,” contains a dashed “Agent Trajectory” box with numbered, alternating “Action” and “Observation” entries, and a dashed “User Pref.” box listing “Difficulty,” “Style,” and “Rubrics,” each with an icon. Orange arrows from these inputs converge on task generation. Beside a small agent and the prompt “What potential problems can this solve?” are two orange output boxes: a question-mark icon with the sample query “Plan path to go back home ?” and a map-pin icon labeled “Ref. Solution.” An orange arrow carries the generated task toward Stage 3.

Stage 3, “Task Curation,” shows an agent replaying a route on another road map with blue location symbols. A dotted blue trail curls from the upper-left agent toward a second agent at lower left; an orange route crosses the map toward a house and points toward the review area. The panel says “Try Replaying.” At upper right are “+ Duplication Filter” and “+ User-Defined Filter” boxes. The text “Query & Solution are feasible” appears by an agent holding a green checked mark; green query and reference-solution icons indicate the verified task and solution.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
